In [[geometry]], the '''small snub icosicosidodecahedron''' or '''snub disicosidodecahedron''' is a [[uniform star polyhedron]], indexed as U<sub>32</sub>. It has 112 faces (100 [[triangle]]s and 12 [[pentagram]]s), 180 edges, and 60 vertices. Its [[stellation]] core is a [[truncated pentakis dodecahedron]]. It also called a '''holosnub icosahedron''', {{math|ß{3,5}.}}

The 40 non-snub triangular faces form 20 coplanar pairs, forming star hexagons that are not quite regular. Unlike most [[Snub polyhedron|snub polyhedra]], it has reflection symmetries.

== Convex hull ==

Its [[convex hull]] is a nonuniform [[truncated icosahedron]].

==Cartesian coordinates==

Let <math>\xi=-\frac32+\frac12\sqrt{1+4\phi}\approx -0.1332396008261379</math> be largest (least negative) zero of the polynomial <math>P=x^2+3x+\phi^{-2}</math>, where <math>\phi</math> is the [[golden ratio]]. Equivalently, <math>
\xi = -2+\sqrt{\phi  + \sqrt{\phi  + \sqrt{\phi  + \cdots}}}\, = -2+\beta </math> where <math>\beta \approx 1.86676039</math> ({{OEIS2C|id= A275828}}) is a root of <math>\beta^2-\beta-\phi=0.</math> Let the point <math>p</math> be given by
:<math>p=
\begin{pmatrix}
        \phi^{-1}\xi+\phi^{-3} \\
        \xi \\
        \phi^{-2}\xi+\phi^{-2}
\end{pmatrix}
</math>.
Let the matrix <math>M</math> be given by
:<math>M=
\begin{pmatrix}
         1/2  & -\phi/2 & 1/(2\phi) \\
         \phi/2   & 1/(2\phi)     & -1/2 \\
         1/(2\phi)     & 1/2  & \phi/2
\end{pmatrix}
</math>.
<math>M</math> is the rotation around the axis <math>(1, 0, \phi)</math>  by an angle of <math>2\pi/5</math>, counterclockwise. Let the linear transformations <math>T_0, \ldots, T_{11}</math> 
be the transformations which send a point <math>(x, y, z)</math> to the [[parity of a permutation|even permutations]] of <math>(\pm x, \pm y, \pm z)</math>  with an [[Parity (mathematics)|even number]] of minus signs. 
The transformations <math>T_i</math> constitute the group of rotational symmetries of a [[regular tetrahedron]].
The transformations <math>T_i M^j</math> <math>(i = 0,\ldots, 11</math>, <math>j = 0,\ldots, 4)</math> constitute the group of rotational symmetries of a [[regular icosahedron]].
Then the 60 points <math>T_i M^j p</math>  are the vertices of a small snub icosicosidodecahedron. The edge length equals <math>-2\xi</math>, the circumradius equals <math>\sqrt{-4\xi-\phi^{-2}}</math>, and the midradius equals <math>\sqrt{-\xi}</math>.

For a small snub icosicosidodecahedron whose edge length is 1,
the circumradius is
:<math>R = \frac12\sqrt{\frac{\xi-1}{\xi}} \approx 1.4581903307387025</math>
Its midradius is
:<math>r = \frac12\sqrt{\frac{-1}{\xi}} \approx 1.369787954633799</math>

The other zero of <math>P</math> plays a similar role in the description of the [[small retrosnub icosicosidodecahedron]].
